note: Why sha256 changed (2026-11-20): capturedSha256 is the SHA-256 of this prompt's text with the trailing spaces cut from 2 line ends (line 4 (2 spaces), line 10 (1 space)) and without the file's final newline; hashing that form of the saved file reproduces it exactly. sha256 is now the SHA-256 of the file bytes, which keep those spaces and the final newline. Cause: trailing spaces plus the trailing newline only; no CRLF, no blank-line collapse, no content change. chars (2563) is the text's length in UTF-16 code units and equals the file's. The one-character gap (chars 2563, file 2562 code points) is not a missing character: line 92 (demo.tsx's "Hello World" heading, which ends in U+1F44B WAVING HAND SIGN) holds one character outside the BMP: one code point, two UTF-16 code units, and chars counts code units. The saved file is the whole captured text (the captured hash reproduces from it), so no re-capture is needed to restore content.
